intro: Retail work builds service orientation, social perceptiveness and persuasion, skills banks, offices and call centers hire for every day. Of the 25 careers below, Tellers match retail workers best at 93%, and 22 of the 25 pay more than retail at the median.
why_it_works: Retail teaches you to handle customers, cash and complaints at the same time, often while on your feet all shift. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.44 out of 5 for retail workers, which is why teller, customer service and clerk roles rank so high. Most of these jobs use the same register, product and people skills with steadier hours. Customer Service Representatives, for example, solve the same problems over the phone. The main gaps are problem solving and operations analysis.
tips: Apply with what you already have: 24 of the 25 matches usually need no extra education.
Count your numbers on your resume, such as sales goals met, cash handled or customers served per shift.
Ask about a shift lead or supervisor role, which builds the problem-solving skills most matches ask for.

faq.q: What jobs can former retail workers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Tellers (93%), Customer Service Representatives (90%) and Door-to-Door Sales Workers, News and Street Vendors, and Related Workers (90%), based on O*NET 31.0. Postal Service Clerks and First-Line Supervisors of Retail Sales Workers (88% each) are also strong options.

faq.q: Which jobs pay more than retail?
faq.a: 22 of the 25 matches pay more than the $34,291 median for the retail workers on this page. Postal Service Clerks earn $62,130, an 81% increase, and Customer Service Representatives earn $44,770, a 31% increase, according to BLS May 2025 data. Sales representatives of services earn $69,990.

faq.q: Can I leave retail without a degree?
faq.a: Yes. 24 of the 25 matches usually need no more education than a retail job, based on O*NET Job Zones. Training happens mostly on the job: tellers usually train for up to 1 month, while customer service representatives can take 6 months to a year to fully learn the role.

faq.q: What retail jobs are a step up from the sales floor?
faq.a: First-Line Supervisors of Retail Sales Workers (88% match) earn a median of $48,520, which is 41% more than the retail workers on this page. If you want to stay in stores, Counter and Rental Clerks (91%) and Parts Salespersons (83%) are other close roles with similar skills.
